item.title: Child among four people killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine
item.description: Falling debris sparked several fires on the outskirts of the Ukrainian capital, in attacks which killed at least four people

item.title: Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general
item.description: In a narrow 50-49 vote, President Trump's former defense lawyer was confirmed as attorney general in a vote early Saturday.

item.title: Senate approves bill to fund government into December
item.description: The measure was approved in a 90 to 6 vote and now goes to the House.

item.title: At least 5 killed and more than 20 injured in Thailand school shooting
item.description: Five school staff members died in the shooting, and 10 people were in critical condition.

item.title: Pentagon revokes security clearance of former Air Force chief
item.description: The Pentagon alleged that former U.S. Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall disclosed sensitive information about Air Force One's capabilities to the media.

item.title: Trump announces $180 million to boost mining education
item.description: President Trump announced over $180 million in grants to boost educational programs for the mining industry, part of a bid to increase critical mineral production.

item.title: NBA player Brandon Clarke died from effects of heroin and cocaine, officials say
item.description: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke died in May from the effects of heroin and cocaine, authorities said Friday.

item.title: Water rationing begins in Puerto Rico amid drought crisis: "It's brutal"
item.description: Puerto Rico's massive rationing measure comes amid a severe drought on top of shortages due to infrastructure issues.

item.title: How a duck's friendship helped a golden retriever overcome health issues
item.description: Justin and Tori Cannarelli of New York almost have a typical American family with their two children and a dog. But they also have one very unique member: a duck.

item.title: Astrophysicist Avi Loeb breaks down Pentagon's 5th batch of UFO files
item.description: The Pentagon has released a new batch of files related to unidentified flying objects. This is now the fifth release under an executive order President Trump signed in January. Astrophysicist Avi Loeb joins with analysis.

item.title: 3 mothers sue to block Texas law requiring Ten Commandments in public schools
item.description: The Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 10 last year, which requires all public school classrooms to display the Ten Commandments.

item.title: Cuban ambassador to the U.N. says island is "suffering a collective punishment" amid U.S. blockade
item.description: Over the past six months or so, Cuba has undergone an unprecedented energy crisis amid President Trump's oil blockade. CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman spoke with Cuban Ambassador to the United Nations Ernesto Soberón Guzman about the challenges his country faces.

item.title: How a duck helped a dog recover from panic attacks, medication that brought him down
item.description: Steve Hartman explores the unique bond between a family's duck and dog.

item.title: Texas parents sue to block mandatory display of Ten Commandments in school classrooms
item.description: As the start of the school year approaches, three Texas mothers are suing to block the mandatory display of the Biblical 10 Commandments in their children's classrooms. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Outer Banks community spending $50 million to save its beachfront economy
item.description: A $50 million effort is underway to restore miles of eroded shoreline in Buxton, a village on one of the barrier islands of North Carolina's Outer Banks.

item.title: Puerto Rico faces severe drought as 180,000 households and businesses forced to ration water
item.description: Puerto Rico is in the midst of its worst drought in decades. Lilia Luciano shares the details.

item.title: Houthi rebels launch new attacks on Saudi-backed troops
item.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels have launched new attacks on Saudi-backed troops in Yemen. The attacks come as Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia sign a mutual defense deal. CBS News national security contributor Samantha Vinograd joins with analysis.

item.title: Trump administration pays out $100 billion in tariff refunds to businesses
item.description: The U.S. government has refunded more than $100 billion to several companies for tariffs they paid after the Supreme Court deemed them illegal, according to a court filing this week. But will consumers see any of that money? CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo joins to discuss.

item.title: North Carolina communities scramble to protect shorelines as erosion eats away at homes
item.description: Communities in North Carolina are scrambling to protect their shorelines as rising sea levels and erosion threaten homes, with many lost in the past few years. Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: July jobs report reveals unexpected loss of 23,000 jobs
item.description: Friday's jobs report showed employers shed jobs last month, rather than adding 95,000 new hires that had been forecast by economists.

item.title: U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, new report shows
item.description: A report released by the Labor Department on Friday showed a loss of 23,000 jobs last month, with many discouraged job seekers leaving the labor force. Kelly O'Grady reports.

item.title: Cassidy backs Blanche for attorney general, clearing way for confirmation
item.description: Louisiana Sen. Bill Cassidy, a Republican, announced he will vote to confirm Todd Blanche for attorney general.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis escalate deadly attacks on Saudi-backed troops
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launch fresh attacks on Saudi-backed government troops, says Yemeni state media, as Cruz says Trump must seek "regime collapse."

item.title: U.S. intel agencies warn Putin could test NATO by authorizing provocative actions
item.description: U.S. intelligence assessments indicate Russia could be increasingly willing to authorize provocative actions on NATO territory, with a goal of testing the alliance, U.S. officials said.

item.title: From Iran's Evin Prison, U.S. citizen Reza Valizadeh releases audio update
item.description: CBS News received a second audio message from journalist Reza Valizadeh, who's been held in Iran's notorious Evin Prison since 2024. He gave an update on the prison conditions and on fellow American Kamran Hekmati, believed to be suffering from a recurring cancer.

item.title: 8/7: CBS Evening News
item.description: Police release footage of In-N-Out shooting; Blanche likely to be confirmed as attorney general.

item.title: Appeals court blocks Trump's White House ballroom, teeing up Supreme Court fight
item.description: A federal appeals court said the White House lacks the authority to unilaterally construct the 90,000-square-foot ballroom. President Trump said the administration will appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Video shows gunman start deadly rampage at Idaho In-N-Out drive-thru
item.description: Three people were killed in the shooting that started at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho.

item.title: Pentagon releases new batch of UFO files: "Did you see that?"
item.description: The Pentagon on Friday released a new batch of documents and images related to UFOs, the fifth disclosure in recent months about the strange encounters.

item.title: DOJ's top prosecutor in LA hires aide with pending battery charge, DUIs
item.description: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli hired former top aide Shawn Lewis to be a federal law enforcement liaison, though Lewis has three prior convictions for driving under the influence and a pending battery charge.
